items.title: The boreal forest is the world's largest terrestrial biome
items.claim: Which is the world's largest forest biome?

options.text: The boreal forest (taiga) — a circumpolar belt across Russia, Canada, Alaska and Scandinavia totalling around 1.5 billion hectares; larger than all tropical rainforests combined and storing more carbon

items.reveal:
Boreal forest covers around 30% of all forest area and stores an estimated 30-40% of terrestrial carbon — much of it in deep peat and permafrost soils. Russia's taiga alone is around 12 million km².

Dominant species: spruce, fir, pine, larch, birch. Wildlife: brown bear, lynx, wolverine, capercaillie, moose. Productivity per hectare is lower than the Amazon, but the area is far larger.

Climate change is intensifying boreal wildfires — Siberia 2019-21, Canada 2023 — releasing carbon and potentially turning some boreal regions into net carbon sources. Permafrost thaw could release vast methane and CO₂.
items.why: The Amazon dominates public attention as 'the lungs of the planet'. The boreal forest is larger, stores more carbon, and is increasingly fire-prone — but receives a fraction of the press coverage.

items.title: Around 90% of LIC employment is informal
items.claim: What share of work is informal in low-income countries?

options.text: Around 90% of employment in LICs and around 60% globally is informal (ILO 2018) — work without legal recognition, social protection or tax registration, totalling around 2 billion workers worldwide

items.reveal:
The International Labour Organization defines informal employment as work without legal recognition or social protection. Concentrations are high in sub-Saharan Africa (around 89% of non-agricultural employment) and South Asia (around 86%).

Main activities: street vending, waste-picking, small-scale agriculture, domestic work, informal manufacturing. Many informal workers are women; many have no fixed workplace.

Keith Hart's 1971 Accra fieldwork coined the modern use of 'informal sector'. ILO Recommendation 204 (2015) framed transition strategies to formal employment.
items.why: Models built on Global North wage labour misrepresent developing economies. The informal sector is not marginal — it is the modal experience of work for two billion people.

items.title: Sea level is rising 3-4 mm per year and accelerating
items.claim: How fast is global mean sea level rising?

options.text: It has been stable for centuries
Satellite altimetry since 1993 shows around 3.4 mm/year average, with the rate accelerating since 2010; IPCC AR6 projects 0.3-1.0 m rise by 2100 depending on emissions

items.reveal:
Thermal expansion of warming ocean water contributes about 40% of recent rise; melt from glaciers and ice sheets the rest. Greenland's mass loss has accelerated from around 50 Gt/year in the 1990s to around 280 Gt/year by 2010s (NASA GRACE data).

Local sea-level rise differs from global. Isostatic rebound (Scotland rising, southern England sinking) and ocean dynamic processes mean some coasts experience faster relative rise.

The AMOC slowdown could redistribute Atlantic sea level — raising it on the US East Coast more than the average.
items.why: Sea-level rise is not uniform and not linear. Local coastal management must plan against regional projections, not a single global figure.
